options.C: Teaching undergraduate students in the classroom

explanation: Clinical informatics directly supports the nurses and patients at the point of care through tools like electronic records and barcode scanners. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h2)

question: What visual sign confirms that an intradermal injection was successfully placed in the dermis?

options.A: A small bleb or blister forms on the skin surface.
options.B: The surrounding skin turns pale and cold to the touch.
options.C: A drop of blood appears at the injection site immediately.
options.D: The medication leaks back out through the needle track.

explanation: The formation of a raised bleb proves the fluid is trapped within the tight dermal skin layers. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following practices regarding alcohol is safest for a nursing mother?

options.A: Consuming alcohol immediately before every single nursing session to relax the baby
options.B: Mixing alcohol directly into infant formula to help the baby sleep through the night
options.C: Drinking large amounts of beer daily because it is traditionally believed to boost milk supply
options.D: Avoiding heavy or frequent drinking and waiting several hours after a drink before nursing

explanation: Alcohol enters breast milk quickly, so minimizing intake and allowing time for the body to clear it protects the infant. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h7)

question: What common, mild-sounding urinary issue during pregnancy can turn into a serious kidney infection (pyelonephritis) if ignored?

options.A: Placental abruption
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Asymptomatic bacteriuria
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Even if bacteria are hanging out in the urine without causing symptoms, leaving them alone gives them a chance to multiply and travel right up to the kidneys.

question: Why is it important to use a combination of methods like interviews and data reviews when assessing a community?

options.A: It prevents community members from speaking directly with nurses
options.B: Government regulations require at least five different reports for every village
options.C: It ensures that every single resident is interviewed individually by a doctor
options.D: It provides a complete and balanced picture of health needs from multiple angles

explanation: Combining statistical data with the lived experiences of community members ensures the true health priorities are identified accurately. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why might a wonder drug that wins lab awards perform poorly in a rural community?

options.A: Patients may struggle with storage requirements or fail to complete the full dosage course
options.B: Doctors prefer writing paper prescriptions instead of using electronic records
options.C: Hospital administrators charge patients identical fees regardless of income
options.D: The government refuses to tax pharmaceutical companies that import the drug

explanation: Real life has challenges! If a drug needs a fridge or a strict 7-day routine, everyday barriers can lower its real-world success.

question: Which four elements form the main building blocks of most nutrients in our diet?

options.A: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen
options.B: Phosphorus, sulfur, chlorine, and magnesium
options.C: Calcium, iron, sodium, and potassium
options.D: Copper, zinc, iodine, and manganese

explanation: Spot on! These four simple elements form the chemical backbone of the carbohydrates, fats, proteins, and nucleic acids we eat every day.

question: Which part of the blastocyst eventually grows into the actual fetus?

options.A: The outer trophoblast
options.B: The blastocoele fluid
options.C: The inner cell mass
options.D: The zona pellucida

explanation: Spot on! The inner cell mass contains the special cells that will form the tissues of the baby itself. Keep up the great work!

question: What is the name of the tough, leather-like outermost layer of the meninges?

options.A: Arachnoid mater
options.B: Pia mater
options.C: Cerebral cortex
options.D: Dura mater

explanation: The dura mater forms the heavy outer protective shield right beneath the skull bones. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h2)

question: A mother on a tight budget needs affordable protein sources for her growing toddlers. Which local foods should the nurse recommend?

options.A: Beans, groundnuts, and local fish
options.B: Processed energy bars from abroad
options.C: Expensive dietary protein powders
options.D: Imported canned salmon and caviar

explanation: Locally available plant and animal proteins like beans, groundnuts, and fish are cost-effective and culturally appropriate options. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of quality care in reproductive health?

options.A: To increase the total number of hospital beds
options.B: To reduce the cost of running the pharmacy
options.C: To shorten the working hours for midwives
options.D: To prevent maternal and newborn complications

explanation: Quality care focuses heavily on keeping mothers and newborns safe from preventable harm during pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h1)

question: A nurse is teaching a patient with poor leg circulation about foot care. Which tip is the most important to include?

options.A: Walk barefoot around the house to toughen your soles
options.B: Soak your feet in warm water for an hour every night
options.C: Check your feet every day for cuts, redness, or blisters
options.D: Cut your toenails into rounded corners with deep edges

explanation: Because poor blood flow slows down healing, even a tiny scratch can turn into a stubborn sore. Daily checks help catch small issues early!

question: In microbiology, what is the main purpose of 'nomenclature'?

options.A: Measuring physical cell size
options.B: Determining antibiotic resistance
options.C: Assigning formal scientific names
options.D: Observing metabolic heat output

explanation: Think of nomenclature as giving official names to microorganisms using established rules, just like giving every newborn a proper name!

question: How do monitoring devices improve nursing documentation?

options.A: By transmitting captured data directly into electronic health records
options.B: By erasing old vital signs every twelve hours
options.C: By forcing nurses to write everything on paper charts first
options.D: By locking all patient data so other staff cannot read it

explanation: Connecting bedside devices to digital records cuts down on manual entry mistakes and saves time. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h1)

question: How can you tell the difference between morning joint stiffness in osteoarthritis versus inflammatory arthritis?

options.A: Osteoarthritis stiffness only affects the upper body joints.
options.B: Osteoarthritis stiffness never happens in the morning hours.
options.C: Osteoarthritis stiffness usually lasts less than thirty minutes.
options.D: Osteoarthritis stiffness gets worse the more the person moves.

explanation: Joint stiffness from wear-and-tear arthritis is brief after waking up, whereas inflammatory arthritis causes stiffness lasting an hour or more. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h3)

question: When you spin a blood sample in a centrifuge, what components make up that thin middle layer called the buffy coat?

options.A: White blood cells and platelets
options.B: Water and dissolved glucose
options.C: Red blood cells and hemoglobin
options.D: Albumin and clotting proteins

explanation: Well done! The buffy coat is that tiny, whitish layer sitting between the clear plasma on top and the heavy red blood cells at the bottom. It holds your infection-fighters (white blood cells) and clotting helpers (platelets).

question: What is one of the key roles of a nurse when acting as a facilitator in community mobilisation?

options.A: Writing laws that fine people who refuse to visit the clinic
options.B: Helping local committees run meetings and prioritize health problems
options.C: Taking over all financial accounts of the local government
options.D: Purchasing private cars for all members of the village council

explanation: As facilitators, nurses guide the process without dominating it, helping residents make their own decisions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h5)

question: As a nurse assessing a patient with severe iron-deficiency anemia, what physical sign are you most likely to spot?

options.A: Pallor of the mucous membranes and nail beds
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes
options.C: Swelling in the hands and lower feet
options.D: Rapid and excessive involuntary weight gain

explanation: Great clinical eye! Low hemoglobin means fewer red blood cells, which makes the inner eyelids, gums, and nail beds look pale.

question: What major reproductive problem is linked to fallopian tube scarring from untreated pelvic infections?

options.A: Premature menopause
options.B: Hypertrophic cervical polyps
options.C: Endometrial hyperplasia
options.D: Ectopic pregnancy and infertility

explanation: Scars in the fallopian tubes can block eggs from traveling normally, leading either to trouble getting pregnant or dangerous ectopic pregnancies.

question: A patient has a heart rate of 180 beats per minute, low blood pressure, and acute chest pain. What is the immediate treatment priority?

options.A: Starting continuous chest compressions
options.B: Synchronized cardioversion
options.C: Oral beta-blocker pills
options.D: Waiting for blood lab results

explanation: An unstable fast rhythm causing low blood pressure and chest pain requires immediate synchronized electrical cardioversion. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h6)

question: Your patient on a nasal cannula complains of a dry, sore throat and a mild nosebleed. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Increase the oxygen flow rate to flush the nasal passages
options.B: Recommend adding humidification to the oxygen setup as prescribed
options.C: Remove the oxygen permanently and document refusal of care
options.D: Switch the patient to a tight-fitting non-rebreather mask

explanation: Dry medical gas can be tough on delicate mucous membranes. Adding moisture (humidification) is the perfect fix to soothe that dryness and irritation.

question: A patient rushes in with severe chest pain, while another has a minor finger cut. According to triage rules, what should you do first?

options.A: Ask both patients to sit in the waiting room together
options.B: Treat the chest pain patient immediately
options.C: Treat the finger cut patient because it will take less time
options.D: Register the finger cut patient first to clear the desk

explanation: You nailed it! Chest pain and trouble breathing point to a high-risk emergency. They always take top priority over minor cuts and scrapes.

question: Which of these is a classic example of a microvascular (small blood vessel) complication of diabetes?

options.A: Diabetic retinopathy affecting the eyes
options.B: Peripheral vascular disease in the legs
options.C: Coronary artery disease leading to angina
options.D: Cerebrospinal stroke affecting speech

explanation: Retinopathy damages the tiny, delicate blood vessels in the eyes, which makes it a classic microvascular complication. You're doing great!

question: Why is it important for nurses to distinguish special cause variation from common cause variation?

options.A: To eliminate all types of patient illness completely
options.B: To avoid overreacting to normal daily fluctuations
options.C: To reduce the number of required nursing shifts
options.D: To ensure that nurses receive larger monthly salaries

explanation: Recognizing common cause prevents staff from chasing random noise, letting them focus their energy on true special cause changes. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is a major time-waster that you will often want to avoid on the ward?

options.A: Searching for missing equipment and supplies
options.B: Asking a colleague to take a routine vital sign
options.C: Reviewing patient charts before medication rounds
options.D: Clustered nursing interventions in a single visit

explanation: Ah, the classic hospital treasure hunt! Wandering around looking for a missing thermometer or BP cuff eats up so much of a 12-hour shift.

question: What should you do if you notice a clinical policy on your ward is outdated or confusing?

options.A: Change the national health laws to match personal preference
options.B: Report the gap through official institutional channels
options.C: Throw away all printed copies of the hospital rulebook
options.D: Keep the information secret from all other staff members

explanation: Using official reporting channels helps management fix and update policies safely without encouraging risky shortcuts on the ward.

question: Why should a community health nurse look at the health needs of a whole group instead of just single patients?

options.A: It helps allocate resources effectively to design meaningful programs
options.B: It guarantees complete eradication of all chronic diseases
options.C: It eliminates the need to ever visit individual households
options.D: It ensures every single citizen receives specialized surgery

explanation: Looking at the big picture helps you focus on what really plagues the population so you can put your limited time and materials to the best possible use!

question: How do assisted living facilities differ from traditional nursing homes?

options.A: Assisted living requires continuous 24-hour physician supervision.
options.B: Nursing homes provide much less medical oversight than assisted living.
options.C: Nursing homes only admit individuals who are completely independent.
options.D: Assisted living focuses more on a home-like setting and independence.

explanation: While nursing homes offer heavy, continuous medical and nursing care, assisted living emphasizes residential comfort and autonomy with lesser medical intervention. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h1)

question: What are the main parts of Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: Surgical sterilization, blood donation drives, and psychiatric isolation
options.B: Emergency treatment, family planning counseling, and reproductive health linkages
options.C: Mandatory legal reporting, punitive counseling, and moral interrogation
options.D: Routine hysterectomy, genetic testing, and long-term foster care referral

explanation: PAC is a complete care package: treat the immediate danger, talk about family planning so it doesn't happen again, and connect them to healthy support networks. Brilliant concept to master!

question: At the end of life, cells struggle to produce enough of which main energy molecule?

options.A: Adenosine triphosphate
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Hemoglobin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Cells need adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to power their everyday work. When oxygen drops at the end of life, ATP production stops too. You've got this!

question: Why is it important for nurses to look beyond purely physical complaints when checking for depression?

options.A: Patients will always directly report feeling sad without prompting
options.B: Physical complaints always disappear once mental health improves
options.C: Depression frequently presents itself disguised as chronic pain or fatigue
options.D: Physical symptoms are completely unrelated to psychological health

explanation: Great job! Patients often show up with body aches, headaches, or extreme tiredness rather than saying they feel sad. Staying alert to this helps us catch what's really going on.

question: What happens during the process of opsonization?

options.A: Blood vessels constrict to stop the spread of an infection
options.B: Antibodies punch direct holes in the cell wall of a virus
options.C: Red blood cells are destroyed to release iron to the tissues
options.D: Pathogens are coated with antibodies to help phagocytes swallow them

explanation: Opsonization is basically tagging an enemy for easy spotting. It's like putting a handle on a pathogen so immune cells like macrophages can easily grab and engulf it!

question: Which combination of symptoms is a major red flag for a postpartum uterine infection?

options.A: Mild swelling in both ankles
options.B: Foul-smelling lochia and fever
options.C: Gradual lightening of lochia color
options.D: Increased appetite and energy

explanation: Spot on! Fever combined with lower tummy pain and bad-smelling lochia are classic signs that the uterus might be infected and needs medical attention.

question: What main event causes urine to leak out in stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Complete blockage of the urethra
options.B: An overactive detrusor muscle spasm
options.C: A sudden urinary tract infection
options.D: Sudden physical pressure on the bladder

explanation: You've got this! Stress incontinence happens when sudden physical pressure—like coughing, laughing, or lifting—pushes urine out because the bladder pressure beats the urethra's grip.

question: Why is allowing residents to make their own choices (autonomy) so important in long-term care?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any nursing staff supervision
options.B: It accelerates the natural healing of acute infections
options.C: It helps preserve resident dignity and psychological health
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of running the facility

explanation: Spot on! When people can still make choices about their day, it boosts their self-worth and keeps their spirits high.

question: Which sign shows that the body can no longer compensate for blood loss?

options.A: A slow and steady decrease in heart rate
options.B: An increase in urine output by the kidneys
options.C: A sharp and sudden drop in blood pressure
options.D: A sudden return of normal skin color

explanation: When compensation fails, the blood pressure crashes. Recognizing this shift is a key nursing skill!

question: What makes paediatric nutrition different from adult nutrition?

options.A: Reducing total daily caloric intake
options.B: Preventing lifestyle diseases like hypertension
options.C: Supporting rapid growth and organ maturation
options.D: Maintaining a stable body weight over time

explanation: You've got this! Children grow fast and their organs are still developing, so they need special nutrients. Adults, on the other hand, mostly just need to maintain their weight. Keep up the great work!

question: What is the main point of using data storytelling in healthcare?

options.A: To increase the daily paperwork burden for floor nurses
options.B: To hide negative hospital audit scores from the public
options.C: To connect numbers with patient care to drive action
options.D: To replace verbal nursing handover reports completely

explanation: You got this! Data storytelling turns boring stats into real human stories that help staff and leaders take action to improve care. Keep it up!

question: What post-procedure instruction should a nurse give to a patient who just received a knee injection?

options.A: Remove the sterile bandage right away and soak in mud
options.B: Run a long distance immediately to spread the medicine
options.C: Take off all clothes and stay in a hot sauna for hours
options.D: Rest the joint and apply ice packs to reduce swelling

explanation: Resting the joint and icing it helps prevent excess irritation and controls post-injection discomfort. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h7)

question: Why is 30 degrees Celsius not considered twice as warm as 15 degrees Celsius?

options.A: Because Celsius measurements have uneven gaps between numbers
options.B: Because the scale lacks a true absolute zero point
options.C: Because thermal energy cannot be measured numerically
options.D: Because temperature is actually measured on a nominal scale

explanation: Without a true zero point where temperature completely disappears, you can't multiply or say something has 'twice as much' heat.

question: Why do community nurses take their analyzed data back to the community for validation?

options.A: To hide negative health statistics from government officials
options.B: To punish local residents who refused to answer survey questions
options.C: To confirm the accuracy of findings with the community members
options.D: To print extra copies of the survey questionnaire

explanation: Validation is all about checking your homework with the people who live there to make sure your conclusions match their everyday reality.

question: Where should a clinical specimen be stored if testing is delayed?

options.A: On an open shelf in the nurses' station
options.B: Inside the staff room food refrigerator
options.C: In a dedicated specimen refrigerator
options.D: Underneath the patient bedside locker

explanation: Specimens requiring delayed processing must go into a specific specimen fridge to avoid contaminating food or clean areas. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h4)

question: What is the best way to check if a patient actually knows how to use a new inhaler after counselling?

options.A: Checking their vital signs twice a day
options.B: Asking the ward supervisor for approval
options.C: Asking the patient to demonstrate how they use it
options.D: Reading the manufacturer instructional manual

explanation: Watching the patient perform the physical technique is the only true way to know if they can apply your instructions correctly.

question: How do tumbu fly larvae usually find their way into the human body?

options.A: By biting the skin like adult mosquitoes
options.B: By direct inhalation of airborne microscopic eggs
options.C: By drinking untreated swamp water
options.D: By active burrowing through the skin from contaminated clothing

explanation: Tumbu flies love laying eggs on clothes drying outside. When those clothes are worn without ironing, the hatched larvae easily penetrate the skin.

question: Which agency coordinates national disaster management in Nigeria?

options.A: Nigerian Union_of Journalists
options.B: Federal Road Safety Corps exclusively
options.C: National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA)
options.D: National Youth Service Corps

explanation: You nailed it! NEMA is the main federal body that handles disaster planning and response across Nigeria.

question: Why must a patient with liver cirrhosis watch their daily sodium intake?

options.A: To prevent fluid from pooling in the abdominal cavity
options.B: To prevent painful muscle cramps in the legs
options.C: To encourage rapid absorption of dietary iron
options.D: To stop sudden spikes in blood glucose levels

explanation: Spot on! Liver issues can cause fluid to collect in the belly (ascites), and eating too much salt makes this swelling much worse.

question: How does Immunoglobulin A (IgA) found in breast milk protect the newborn infant?

options.A: It regulates the baby's body temperature in cold environments
options.B: It coats the intestinal lining to stop germs from entering the body
options.C: It stimulates the baby's pancreas to release digestive enzymes
options.D: It directly increases the infant's red blood cell production

explanation: Secretory IgA forms a protective barrier along the baby's gut, preventing harmful bacteria and viruses from invading. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h3)

question: Which group of professionals makes up the core mental health team?

options.A: Pharmacists, physiotherapists, and laboratory technicians
options.B: Surgeons, anesthetists, and theater nurses
options.C: Psychiatrists, nurses, social workers, and occupational therapists
options.D: Hospital administrators, accountants, and security officers

explanation: Spot on! Good mental health care brings together medical, nursing, social, and daily living expertise.

question: When would a manual blood pressure check with a stethoscope be a better choice than a digital machine?

options.A: When the patient is checking their own pressure at home
options.B: When the patient has a very irregular heartbeat
options.C: When the hospital ward is completely quiet
options.D: When you are in a rush during a busy shift

explanation: Digital machines struggle to calculate properly when the heart rhythm jumps all over the place. That's when your manual auscultation skills shine!

question: You test fluid pulled from a newly placed NG tube and find a pH of 4.0. What does this tell you?

options.A: The patient is experiencing severe lung infection.
options.B: The tube is correctly placed in the stomach.
options.C: The tube is coiled inside the patient's esophagus.
options.D: The tube has accidentally entered the lungs.

explanation: Stomach acid is nice and acidic, usually sitting between pH 1.0 and 5.5. A pH of 4.0 is a great sign you are in the right spot!

question: A doctor orders 250 mg of a drug. The vial contains 500 mg of powder. The instructions state to add 2 mL of sterile water to yield 500 mg per 2 mL. How many milliliters should the nurse withdraw?

options.A: 1 mL
options.B: 4 mL
options.C: 0.5 mL
options.D: 2 mL

explanation: If 500 mg is in 2 mL, then half the dose (250 mg) is found in half the volume, which is 1 mL. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h3)

question: Why do doctors often order a Complete Blood Count (CBC) when investigating stubborn fatigue?

options.A: To measure the exact resting metabolic rate
options.B: To quantify circulating central nervous system neurotransmitters
options.C: To detect abnormal levels of thyroid hormones
options.D: To check for anemia and rule out infection

explanation: Spot on! A CBC helps us check red blood cells for anemia and white blood cells for hidden infections, giving us clues about why the patient feels so drained.

question: Why should nurses treat a patient's fear as a serious clinical issue?

options.A: It allows the nurse to discharge the patient much faster.
options.B: It removes the need to administer prescribed medications.
options.C: It helps the nurse deliver targeted and empathetic interventions.
options.D: It ensures the patient will never ask questions about surgery.

explanation: You got it! Acknowledging fear as a real medical concern lets us give patients the exact emotional and physical backup they need to heal.

question: A 16-year-old girl drops out of school due to an unplanned pregnancy. What long-term impact is she most likely to face?

options.A: Immediate government employment
options.B: Automatic university admission
options.C: Lifelong economic hardship
options.D: Complete immunity from malaria

explanation: Interrupting education early often limits future career opportunities, leading to long-term financial struggles. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h2)

question: How does an additive drug interaction work?

options.A: The combined effect equals the sum of individual effects
options.B: The drugs completely destroy each other in the bloodstream
options.C: The combined effect is lower than either single drug
options.D: The combined effect is much greater than individual effects

explanation: An additive effect is straightforward: 1 + 1 = 2! The drugs simply add their normal effects together without extra superpowers.

question: Why is risk pooling so important for making healthcare affordable?

options.A: It ensures that sick individuals do not bear the full financial burden alone
options.B: It allows hospitals to buy medical equipment without paying taxes
options.C: It guarantees that doctors receive higher salaries every year
options.D: It stops insurance companies from hiring administrative staff

explanation: Spot on! Spreading financial risk across a big group makes healthcare costs manageable instead of wiping out a single patient's savings.

question: Why is a slightly lower hemoglobin level accepted during the second trimester?

options.A: Maternal bone marrow becomes temporarily suppressed
options.B: Red blood cell production completely stops temporarily
options.C: Greater plasma volume expansion occurs during this period
options.D: Fetal iron demands are lowest at this stage of growth

explanation: Spot on! The body makes a lot more fluid (plasma) during the second trimester. This extra fluid dilutes the red blood cells, which naturally lowers the hemoglobin reading without meaning she's losing blood.

question: Why is randomization so important when assigning patients to study groups?

options.A: It gives every participant an equal chance of ending up in any group
options.B: It ensures that only the oldest patients get the new treatment
options.C: It makes the research paper shorter to write
options.D: It allows the nurse to choose which patient needs the therapy most

explanation: Randomization spreads patient differences evenly across groups, preventing researcher bias from messing up the final results. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h2)

question: A peanut allergy patient feels completely fine 30 minutes after getting epinephrine and asks to go home immediately. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Perform allergy skin prick testing before allowing the patient to leave
options.B: Explain that prolonged observation is required to watch for secondary symptom flare-ups
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for oral antihistamines
options.D: Administer a second dose of epinephrine just to prevent any future problems

explanation: Don't let them rush off just yet! Because of the risk of biphasic reactions, patients need to stay in the hospital for observation for a few hours.

question: Why do we have a structured referral system between primary clinics and large teaching hospitals?

options.A: Preventing tertiary hospitals from ever seeing complex cases
options.B: Ensuring patients receive the appropriate level of care efficiently
options.C: Increasing the financial cost of routine patient visits
options.D: Keeping patients in primary clinics for as long as possible

explanation: Exactly! The referral system makes sure patients get sent to the right facility that has the exact equipment and specialists they need.

question: When calculating the incidence of a disease, what goes on top (the numerator)?

options.A: The number of new cases developed during a period
options.B: The entire population living in the community
options.C: The number of patients who recovered completely
options.D: The total number of people who died from old age

explanation: Great job! The numerator in an incidence formula always focuses strictly on the newly diagnosed cases.

question: Which symptom is a classic warning sign of dangerous preeclampsia getting worse?

options.A: Complete inability to swallow liquids
options.B: Severe frontal headache and hyperreflexia
options.C: Total loss of hearing in both ears
options.D: Sudden uncontrollable shaking of the feet

explanation: Always look out for this in clinicals! Brain irritation from high blood pressure and swelling often shows up as a bad headache and jumpy reflexes.

question: What makes a hybrid computer special?

options.A: It can only function inside a hospital operating theatre
options.B: It combines the input and output features of both analog and digital systems
options.C: It relies entirely on manual data entry without electricity
options.D: It operates without a central processing unit

explanation: Think of hybrid as the best of both worlds! It takes continuous physical signals and turns them into digital numbers so we can process them easily.

question: What is the general rule for how women with vulval varicose veins give birth?

options.A: A scheduled caesarean section is required in every single case
options.B: Labor must be induced early at thirty-six weeks gestation
options.C: Vaginal delivery is usually safe and successful for most women
options.D: Forceps delivery must be used to protect the perineal blood vessels

explanation: Good news! Having vulval varicosities doesn't automatically mean a C-section. Most mothers have safe, normal vaginal deliveries with proper supportive care.

question: Which food choice is generally NOT recommended when mixing crushed medication for an infant?

options.A: A small taste of flavored pudding
options.B: A spoonful of sweet applesauce
options.C: Daily milk or formula bottle feeds
options.D: A small drop of fruit puree

explanation: Mixing drugs into routine milk feeds can cause the infant to reject their primary nutrition if the taste changes. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h6)

question: Why do doctors order genetic tests like FISH or karyotyping for blood cancers?

options.A: To find the patient's blood group for a transfusion
options.B: To find specific chromosome changes and gene mutations
options.C: To measure how much blood was lost in surgery
options.D: To see how fast red blood cells settle in a tube

explanation: Looking at the genetic makeup of the cancer cells helps the medical team figure out the best treatment plan for the patient.

question: Why is family planning counseling important early in the postpartum period?

options.A: Traditional birth control methods never work after childbirth
options.B: Women cannot get pregnant while breastfeeding
options.C: Ovulation can happen before her monthly period returns
options.D: Hormonal contraceptives must start on delivery day

explanation: Many women are surprised to learn they can release an egg and get pregnant again before they even see their first postpartum period!

question: Why is it so important to keep raw meat away from foods you are ready to eat?

options.A: To prevent cross-contamination of harmful bacteria
options.B: To improve the overall taste of cooked dishes
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of meal storage
options.D: To speed up the cooking process on the stove

explanation: Keeping raw items separate stops germs from jumping onto food items that won't be cooked again before eating.

question: Which of these is NOT a good quality for a clinical recommendation based on research data?

options.A: Being directly supported by the findings of the study
options.B: Being clear and easy for frontline nurses to understand
options.C: Being realistic about the equipment available in the clinic

options.B: International donors legally mandate that local taxes be abolished
options.C: Government health budgets often fall short of recommended funding targets
options.D: Citizens prefer foreign organizations over government clinics

explanation: When national funding isn't enough to cover public health needs, external donations step in to help keep clinics open and running.

question: What is the main trigger that causes blood vessels in the newborn lungs to relax and open?

options.A: Gravity pulling fluid downward
options.B: The sudden release of adrenal hormones
options.C: The physical drop in environmental temperature
options.D: Exposure to oxygen from the first breath

explanation: Oxygen is a powerful natural vasodilator; when air enters the lungs, the sudden oxygen increase relaxes the pulmonary blood vessels. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h3)

question: What physical exam finding is typically linked to pelvic infections like salpingitis?

options.A: Painless rigidity of the abdominal wall
options.B: Enlargement of the spleen
options.C: Cervical motion tenderness
options.D: Absent bowel sounds in all quadrants

explanation: During a pelvic exam, moving the cervix stretches those inflamed tissues, causing sharp pain.

question: What is the main job of freshwater snails in the life cycle of schistosomes?

options.A: They transport the parasite permanently out of aquatic environments.
options.B: They consume human waste to reduce overall environmental egg counts.
options.C: They serve as the definitive host where adult worms reproduce sexually.
options.D: They act as intermediate hosts where asexual multiplication occurs.

explanation: Think of the snail as a busy factory! Inside the snail, a single parasite multiplies into thousands of infectious cercariae. Neat biology fact for your clinical notes!

question: Why is proper clinical notes sent along with an emergency referral so important?

options.A: It acts as a formal receipt for community transport payment
options.B: It prevents the receiving hospital from asking any questions
options.C: It provides essential clinical history to speed up hospital treatment
options.D: It gives the referral team legal protection against lawsuits

explanation: You nailed it! Sharing past findings, treatments given, and vitals helps the hospital team jump right into action without wasting precious time repeating tests.

question: Why must nurses strictly avoid giving aspirin or ibuprofen to a yellow fever patient?

options.A: They cause the body temperature to spike dangerously high
options.B: They increase the risk of severe bleeding and hemorrhage
options.C: They destroy remaining healthy cells in the liver and kidneys
options.D: They neutralize the effectiveness of prescribed intravenous fluids

explanation: That's right! Yellow fever messes with normal blood clotting, and drugs like ibuprofen make bleeding way worse. Always check before giving pain meds! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h6)

question: Which of these tasks is the main job of the scrub nurse during an operation?

options.A: Positioning the operating table and adjusting surgical lights
options.B: Tracking sponge counts and handing instruments to the surgeon
options.C: Managing patient billing and specimen transport logistics
options.D: Completing the electronic health record and nursing notes

explanation: The scrub nurse stays sterile right at the field, passing tools smoothly and keeping a careful count of sponges and instruments.

question: Why must a nursing unit's objectives match the wider hospital vision?

options.A: It ensures every department pulls in the same direction.
options.B: It guarantees an increase in annual government funding.
options.C: It completely removes the need for nursing supervisors.
options.D: It allows nurses to change hospital policies at will.

explanation: When everyone shares the same focus, different departments work together smoothly instead of working against each other.

question: Why is it so important for the body to keep producing hCG right after the embryo implants?

options.A: It directly softens the pelvic bones to prepare for eventual childbirth
options.B: It stimulates the fetal heart to begin beating inside the gestational sac
options.C: It forces the corpus luteum to keep producing progesterone and prevents menstruation
options.D: It stops the maternal immune system from ever recognizing the fetus

explanation: Spot on! hCG sends a vital signal to keep progesterone flowing, which stops the womb lining from shedding so the pregnancy can continue safely.

question: How long should you rub your hands together when using an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: One to two minutes
options.B: Five to ten seconds
options.C: Twenty to thirty seconds
options.D: Five full minutes

explanation: That is correct! Taking at least 20 to 30 seconds ensures you cover all surfaces of your hands and give the sanitizer enough time to kill the germs.

question: Which of the following is NOT measured by GDP or GNP?

options.A: Total market value of goods
options.B: Total income generated by businesses
options.C: Overall population health and happiness
options.D: Monetary value of services rendered

explanation: GDP and GNP only measure money and production. They don't capture human well-being, happiness, or social health directly.

question: What makes a person's blood type classified as Rh-positive?

options.A: The lack of any proteins on the cell surface
options.B: The presence of anti-Rh antibodies in the plasma
options.C: The presence of the D antigen on red blood cells
options.D: The ability to donate blood to anyone safely

explanation: The main determinant of Rh-positive status is finding the D antigen on the surface of the red blood cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h3)

question: A patient having an autoimmune flare has extreme fatigue and stiff joints. What is a great initial nursing action?

options.A: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent swelling in the joints
options.B: Help the patient plan daily activities and schedule mandatory rest periods
options.C: Advise the patient to stop taking all prescribed medications immediately
options.D: Encourage the patient to push through the fatigue with rigorous exercise

explanation: Energy conservation and pacing are wonderful nursing interventions. We help clients save their strength for what matters most without burning out.

question: A teenager leaves a village for the city because friends talk about how easy it is to make money at the motor park. What kind of factor is this?

options.A: A push factor
options.B: An institutional mandate
options.C: A pull factor
options.D: A physiological stressor

explanation: You got it! The bright promise of making money acts like a magnet, 'pulling' the child toward city life.

question: How long should you wash your hands with soap and water before handling food?

options.A: Twenty seconds
options.B: Five seconds
options.C: Ten minutes
options.D: Two minutes

explanation: Washing for at least twenty seconds gives soap and friction enough time to lift away dirt and germs. Great job keeping things clean!

question: A grand multiparous woman arrives at the labor ward in active labor. What is the very first priority action you should take as the nurse?

options.A: Instruct the patient to push forcefully with every contraction
options.B: Set up an IV line and take blood for crossmatching
options.C: Prepare the patient for an immediate routine cesarean section
options.D: Administer general anesthesia to prevent any labor pain

explanation: Since heavy bleeding is a major risk for her, getting an IV line ready and having matched blood on standby before things get complicated is a true lifesaver.

question: What is the main advantage of facility-based quarantine over home quarantine for arriving travelers?

options.A: It allows quarantined persons to continue going to their normal workplaces.
options.B: It removes the need for any infection control supplies whatsoever.
options.C: It guarantees that travelers will never catch any other illness.
options.D: It allows health workers to monitor symptoms and test individuals more easily.

explanation: Centralized facilities allow medical staff to perform regular temperature checks and administer diagnostic tests efficiently. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h4)

question: What major change did the Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 introduce regarding resident management?

options.A: It removed all requirements for regular state health inspections
options.B: It placed severe restrictions on the use of physical and chemical restraints
options.C: It encouraged facilities to lock residents in rooms for safety
options.D: It mandated that all residents must take daily sedative medications

explanation: The 1987 law stepped in because restraints were often used just to make life easier for staff rather than keeping patients safe. The law heavily cracked down on this practice!

question: Which of the following is a common physical sign frequently experienced by a grieving person?

options.A: Permanent loss of hearing
options.B: High fever and skin rashes
options.C: Extreme fatigue and sleep changes
options.D: Sudden increase in muscle mass

explanation: Grief heavily drains physical energy, frequently causing profound fatigue and trouble sleeping. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h4)

question: What does client-centered care primarily turn the patient into?

options.A: An active partner in their own health decisions
options.B: A primary financial contributor to the ward
options.C: An unofficial clinical researcher
options.D: An independent supervisor of hospital staff

explanation: Client-centered care values the patient's voice, making them an active participant alongside the healthcare team. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h3)

question: In conductive hearing loss, what is the main issue preventing sound from being heard clearly?

options.A: Hair cells inside the cochlea are permanently destroyed
options.B: The auditory nerve is completely severed from the brain
options.C: Sound waves are blocked from reaching the inner ear
options.D: Electrical signals bypass the brain's temporal lobe

explanation: You've got this! Conductive hearing loss simply means something is blocking sound waves from traveling through the outer or middle ear. Think of it like a blocked pathway.

question: What type of cartilage connects the bones in a symphysis joint, like the pubic symphysis?

options.A: Elastic cartilage
options.B: Calcified bone matrix
options.C: Fibrocartilage
options.D: Dense fibrous connective tissue

explanation: Spot on! Symphysis joints use tough pads of fibrocartilage to absorb shocks while giving just a tiny bit of flexibility.

question: Why is it important for hospital leadership to show staff that audit data leads to real changes?

options.A: It proves that managers do all the heavy work on the ward
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future ward meetings
options.C: It motivates staff to keep participating honestly in quality data collection
options.D: It stops patients from asking questions about their treatment

explanation: When nurses see that their reports actually solve real ward problems, they feel valued and stay excited to help make things better.

question: Why is seeing a patient at home more revealing than seeing them in a hospital clinic?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any health teaching
options.B: It gives the nurse access to advanced laboratory equipment
options.C: It shows their true daily living conditions and family dynamics
options.D: It forces the patient to follow medical advice strictly

explanation: The home environment exposes real-life challenges like food storage, safety hazards, and family support systems that clinics hide. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h1)

question: Which food source gives us iron that our bodies can absorb the easiest?

options.A: Inorganic iron found in mineral spring water
options.B: Heme iron found in animal products
options.C: Non-heme iron found in leafy green vegetables
options.D: Fortified iron found in refined white flour

explanation: You got it! Heme iron from meats, fish, and poultry is easily taken up by your body compared to plant sources.

question: Why must nurses specifically ask patients about over-the-counter painkillers during a medication review?

options.A: Patients often do not consider non-prescription drugs as 'real' medications to report
options.B: Non-prescription drugs completely cure all forms of arthritis
options.C: Over-the-counter drugs have no side effects on bones or joints
options.D: Patients are legally prohibited from taking pain relievers at home

explanation: Spot-on! Patients often forget to mention everyday painkillers they buy over the counter, even though they can cause side effects or interact with other drugs.

question: A mother brings her toddler to a primary health care clinic with watery diarrhea and sunken eyes. According to standing orders for gastroenteritis, what is the priority intervention?

options.A: Wait for a visiting medical consultant to arrive next week before acting
options.B: Refer the child straight to a tertiary teaching hospital for surgery
options.C: Assess hydration status and initiate rehydration therapy immediately
options.D: Prescribe strong sleeping pills to keep the child quiet during the day

explanation: Primary care standing orders for gastroenteritis prioritize checking hydration and starting oral rehydration or fluids to prevent shock. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h5)

question: When is a retrospective nursing audit done?

options.A: After the patient has been discharged from the hospital
options.B: While the patient is actively receiving treatment on the ward
options.C: Before the patient is even admitted to the emergency room
options.D: During the exact moment a surgical operation is happening

explanation: You got it! Think of 'retrospective' as looking backward—these audits review completed medical records after the patient has already left the facility.

question: In infection control, what do we mean by the 'source of infection'?

options.A: The specific place or object from which an infectious agent passes to a host
options.B: Any medication used to treat a bacterial disease
options.C: The permanent habitat where a microorganism always multiplies
options.D: The specific immune response mounted by a healthy patient

explanation: Think of the source as the direct hand-off point—it's where the germ jumps from to land on the patient. You've got this!

question: What is the main goal of evaluating population health programs?

options.A: To write promotional brochures for the local government ministry
options.B: To find staff members to blame when a project runs out of money
options.C: To increase the cost of medical services for community residents
options.D: To determine whether the health interventions actually achieved their intended goals

explanation: Evaluation measures the real-world impact of health programs so nurses know what is working and what needs improvement. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h7)

question: Why is regular exercise and an active lifestyle good for a patient's bone health?

options.A: Lifestyle habits have no direct connection to skeletal strength
options.B: Weight-bearing exercise stimulates bone density and strengthens supporting muscles
options.C: Sedentary habits automatically increase vitamin D absorption in the skin
options.D: Exercise prevents all forms of genetic joint disease completely

explanation: Exactly right! Putting gentle physical stress on bones through movement tells the body to build stronger, denser bones.

question: An elderly patient with poor eyesight and mild forgetfulness is prescribed a new blood pressure pill. What is your best nursing strategy to help them remember?

options.A: Hand over a dense medical journal article explaining the drug's mechanism
options.B: Instruct a family member to administer the pills without involving the patient
options.C: Provide large-print written instructions and suggest a pill organizer box
options.D: Tell the patient to memorize the dosing schedule without any external aids

explanation: Spot on! Practical tools like big print and pill boxes make managing medications at home much easier and safer for older adults.

question: What exactly is a sampling frame?

options.A: The statistical formula used to calculate sample size
options.B: The physical list of all eligible members in the target population
options.C: The timeline created for data collection in the ward
options.D: The equipment used to measure vital signs in a study

explanation: Great job! Think of a sampling frame as your actual directory or register (like a ward admission book) from which you pick your participants.

question: What do we call the entire group of people a researcher actually wants to study?

options.A: Population
options.B: Parameter
options.C: Variable
options.D: Sample

explanation: That's correct! The 'population' is the total group you are interested in—like all diabetic patients in Lagos State. Keep up the great flow!

question: Why do healthcare workers usually resist new changes in the workplace?

options.A: Laziness and a general refusal to work hard
options.B: A normal defense mechanism against the unknown
options.C: An inadequate level of basic clinical training
options.D: A deliberate attempt to sabotage patient safety

explanation: You're doing great! Resistance isn't about being lazy—it's just a natural human reaction when our daily routine gets shaken up by the unknown.

question: What is the most common reason drug toxicity happens in a patient?

options.A: Drinking plenty of water throughout the day
options.B: Excessively high blood levels of the medication
options.C: Taking the medication exactly as prescribed
options.D: Eating fresh fruits right after taking a pill

explanation: Toxicity simply means too much of a good thing! It happens when the drug concentration in the bloodstream climbs past the safe zone.

question: What kind of air pressure do they use inside an operating room to keep outside hallway air from rushing in?

options.A: Neutral pressure
options.B: Positive pressure
options.C: Negative pressure
options.D: Vacuum pressure

explanation: Think of positive air pressure like a gentle wind blowing outward whenever the door opens, keeping the dirty hallway air away from the clean theatre.

question: Which type of healthcare standard looks closely at a hospital's physical environment and tools?

options.A: Outcome standards
options.B: Financial standards
options.C: Process standards
options.D: Structure standards

explanation: Structure standards check the setup of the hospital—things like building conditions, working equipment, and the staff's qualifications before care even starts.

question: What must happen to qualitative data, like recorded patient interviews, before analysis?

options.A: They must be transcribed word-for-word into written text
options.B: They must be translated into three different foreign languages
options.C: They must be deleted immediately to protect hospital files
options.D: They must be converted entirely into bar charts and graphs

explanation: Audio recordings of interviews need to be written out as text transcripts so researchers can read, code, and analyze the themes. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h2)

question: What should you do if a vulnerable family is unable to reach a goal in their care plan?

options.A: Assume they are lazy and stop visiting them forever
options.B: Report the parents to the police for non-cooperation
options.C: Discharge the family and refuse further help
options.D: Re-evaluate the plan, listen to their challenges, and adjust together

explanation: Exactly! Unmet goals usually mean the plan was too difficult or obstacles got in the way. Team up with the family to tweak your approach!

question: Which clinical sign is a nurse most likely to observe in a patient experiencing moderate dehydration?

options.A: Cold sweating and rapid weight gain
options.B: Dry mucous membranes and concentrated dark urine
options.C: Swollen ankles and elevated blood pressure
options.D: Excessive saliva production and frequent urination

explanation: When the body lacks water, it conserves fluid by reducing urine output (making it dark) and drying out mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T005#GNS227_U1_T005_h7)

question: What is the main protective job of the Golgi tendon reflex?

options.A: Causing a muscle to contract harder when it is stretched too fast
options.B: Helping the body maintain balance when standing on one foot
options.C: Preventing injury by causing an overly tense muscle to relax
options.D: Sensing hot temperatures to trigger a quick withdrawal response

explanation: Think of this reflex as a safety brake. If a muscle is pulling with too much dangerous force, it tells the muscle to relax so the tendon doesn't tear.

question: Which graph is better than a pie chart for tracking patient recovery over several months?

options.A: A pie chart
options.B: A line graph
options.C: A raw data list
options.D: A frequency table

explanation: You got it! Line graphs are your best friend for showing changes and trends over time.
